title: Finite qcqs open–closed scheme trees and module branch composites
statement: A finite qcqs open–closed tree with root $X$ is inductively a single qcqs scheme $X$, or a qcqs scheme $X$ with two such trees rooted at $U$ and $Z$ and complementary quasi-compact open and closed immersions $j:U\to X$ and $i:Z\to X$. Schemes and morphisms are those of [def-pc-scheme], quasi-compactness is [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], quasi-separatedness is [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], open and closed immersions are [def-weil-open-immersion] and [def-weil-closed-immersion], and quasi-compact morphisms are [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both empty schemes and one-vertex trees are permitted. A vertex path is either the root path or a path in one child followed by its edge; its map to $X$ is the actual composite of these scheme morphisms. A leaf path ends at a one-vertex subtree. For a commutative condensed ring $R$ and its pulled-back rings $R_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], let $e_p^R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_W}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$ be the path composite on module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]: the root path gives the identity, an open step appends $j_!$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and a closed step appends $i_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. These are the exact edge functors of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed].
